html:
A planned city in northwest India, built from the early 1950s to replace Lahore as the capital of Indian Punjab after Partition gave Lahore to Pakistan. The Swiss-French architect Le Corbusier drew its master plan.

Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru wanted a city "unfettered by the traditions of the past", a symbol of the new nation's faith in the future. An American plan by Albert Mayer came first; after his partner died, Le Corbusier took over in 1951, working with Pierre Jeanneret, Maxwell Fry and Jane Drew. The city is laid out in a grid of self-contained sectors, each with its own shops, schools and green spaces, with wide roads between.

Its Capitol Complex, with the High Court, Secretariat and Assembly in raw concrete, is one of the great works of modernist architecture and a World Heritage Site since 2016. The city also has Nek Chand's Rock Garden, built secretly from waste. In 1966, when Punjab was split, Chandigarh became a union territory and the shared capital of Punjab and Haryana. It inspired other modernist capitals, such as Louis Kahn's parliament at Dhaka.
